body:
Agent commands that are added by editing an existing comment can look accepted but do not run the requested action.

Plain-language problem:

A user may post a comment, then edit it a few minutes later to add a command such as `@sepo-agent /fix-pr` or `@sepo-agent /review`. The edited comment wakes the agent entrypoint, the router can parse the command, and the agent may even add an eyes reaction. However, the downstream PR action is currently guarded with `github.event.action != 'edited'`, so the requested job is skipped. From the user's point of view, the agent appeared to notice the request but then nothing happened.

This is confusing because there is no visible explanation on the PR telling the user that commands added by editing a comment are not allowed to launch PR-modifying actions.

Desired behavior:

- If edited comments should remain blocked for safety, the portal should not silently acknowledge them as actionable. It should post a short explanation such as: "I noticed this command on an edited comment, but PR-modifying actions only run from new comments. Please post a new comment with the command."
- Alternatively, support edited comments safely by detecting that a trusted user added a valid explicit command and dispatching the requested action exactly once.
- Avoid adding reactions or status signals that imply the action is running when the downstream action will be skipped.
- Add tests covering edited issue comments and edited PR comments for explicit `/review` and `/fix-pr` commands.

Why this matters:

This failure mode is easy to hit when users refine a comment after posting it. The current behavior creates a silent no-op and makes it hard to tell whether the agent is broken, waiting, or deliberately refusing to run.

@sepo-agent /answer sorry the simple fix should be just allow that for fix pr route?

Yes, for `/fix-pr` specifically that’s probably the better simple policy.

I would not just remove the edited-event guard wholesale, though. The current skip is the `fix-pr` job condition in [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L1155-L1163). Safer minimal shape:

- allow `/fix-pr` when the comment is new, as today
- also allow `/fix-pr` when an edited PR comment newly added that explicit route
- compare against `changes.body.from` so repeated edits to the same `/fix-pr` comment do not rerun it
- leave `/review` blocked/explained unless we separately decide edited review requests are okay too

So the fix is “allow edited `/fix-pr` route,” but with an idempotency predicate, not a blanket `github.event.action == edited` bypass.
